NSF-101.title: No administrator permission
NSF-101.summary: NSF Shield must run as administrator to load the network driver (WinDivert).
causes: The app was opened as a normal user.
Windows asked 'Do you want to allow this app to make changes?' and 'No' was chosen.
steps: Close the app.
Right-click NSFShield.exe and choose 'Run as administrator'.
In the installed version, turning on Settings → 'Start with Windows' makes it start as administrator without asking next time.
NSF-101.detect: Checked when the app starts and during the Find Problems scan.

NSF-102.title: Engine files are missing
NSF-102.summary: A file of the selected engine (goodbyedpi.exe, winws.exe, cygwin1.dll, ciadpi.exe or a WinDivert file) was not found in the bin folder.
causes: An antivirus program quarantined or deleted the files.
The zip file was not fully extracted.
The files were moved or deleted manually.
steps: Check your antivirus quarantine list and restore the NSF Shield files.
Report the file to Microsoft as a false positive ('Report false positive' button → microsoft.com/wdsi/filesubmission); once it is reviewed and approved, Defender stops warning.
Verify that the files are official: Troubleshooting → Full check compares the SHA-256 hashes on the 'File integrity' line with the official GoodbyeDPI 0.2.3rc3 release.
Extract the zip file again, completely, into a folder (or run the installer again).
Last resort: add only the NSF Shield folder (not the whole disk or Downloads) to the antivirus exclusions
NSF-102.detect: The files are checked when protection starts and during the Find Problems scan.

NSF-103.title: The app is running from a temporary folder
NSF-103.summary: The app was started from inside the zip file or from the Temp folder. Settings may be lost; the background service and startup task break.
causes: The zip file was opened by double-clicking and the app was started directly from inside it.
The app is in a temporary place such as Downloads/Temp.
steps: Exit the app.
Right-click the zip file and choose 'Extract All'.
Put the folder in a permanent place (e.g. C:\Program Files\NSF Shield or Documents).
Run the app from its new location.
NSF-103.detect: The folder path is checked when the app starts.

NSF-104.title: Settings cannot be saved
NSF-104.summary: The app cannot write to its 'data' folder; your changes are lost when it closes.
causes: The folder is read-only or in a protected location.
The disk is full.
The 'Controlled folder access' feature of Windows Security blocks writing.
steps: Move the app to a writable folder.
Allow NSF Shield in Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → Ransomware protection → Controlled folder access.
Free up disk space.

NSF-105.title: Engine files could not be verified
NSF-105.summary: A file of the selected engine is not identical to its official release (GoodbyeDPI 0.2.3rc3, zapret v72.13 or ByeDPI 0.17.3, SHA-256). For safety, protection was not started.
causes: The file was corrupted during download.
A program or a person changed the file.
An antivirus tried to 'clean' the file and damaged it.
steps: Download NSF Shield again from the official release page (GitHub) and extract it into a new folder.
If you use the installed version, repair or reinstall it.
If the problem persists, add the file name and hash from the log to your issue report.
NSF-105.detect: Every time protection starts, the file hashes are compared with the official hashes built into the program.

NSF-106.title: The last shutdown was unexpected
NSF-106.summary: NSF Shield did not close properly last time. Protection in app mode may have stopped together with the app; it has started again now.
causes: The app crashed because of an error.
It was force-closed from Task Manager or by another program.
There was a power cut, or the computer froze and was turned off.
steps: You do not need to do anything; if it happens often, add the log and the data\last-crash.txt file to your issue report (Troubleshooting → Support package).
NSF-106.detect: When the app starts, it checks whether the previous run closed properly.

NSF-201.title: The WinDivert driver could not be loaded
NSF-201.summary: The network driver that GoodbyeDPI uses to capture packets could not be started.
causes: An antivirus program is blocking the driver.
A different WinDivert driver version loaded by another program is still in memory.
Windows is waiting for a restart to finish a pending update.
steps: Press the Troubleshooting → 'Reset everything' button.
Restart the computer.
If an antivirus is blocking it, follow the steps of NSF-204 (report the false positive first).
Start protection again.
NSF-201.detect: Detected from GoodbyeDPI's 'Error opening filter' output.

NSF-202.title: Driver files not found
NSF-202.summary: GoodbyeDPI reported that it could not find WinDivert.dll or WinDivert64.sys.
causes: An antivirus deleted or quarantined the file.
The package was extracted incompletely.
steps: Restore the files from the antivirus quarantine.
Report the file to Microsoft as a false positive ('Report false positive' button → microsoft.com/wdsi/filesubmission); once it is reviewed and approved, Defender stops warning.
Verify that the files are official: Troubleshooting → Full check compares the SHA-256 hashes on the 'File integrity' line with the official GoodbyeDPI 0.2.3rc3 release.
Extract the zip again.
Last resort: add only the NSF Shield folder (not the whole disk or Downloads) to the antivirus exclusions
NSF-202.detect: Detected from the 'were not found' text in GoodbyeDPI's output.

NSF-203.title: The driver signature could not be verified
NSF-203.summary: Windows did not accept the digital signature of the WinDivert driver.
causes: Windows is very old and does not support SHA-2 signatures.
The driver file is corrupted.
Driver signature enforcement settings were changed.
steps: Install all updates with Windows Update.
Download and extract the package again.
Restart the computer.
NSF-203.detect: Detected from the 'digital signature' text in GoodbyeDPI's output.

NSF-204.title: The driver was blocked by security software
NSF-204.summary: Your antivirus program prevented the WinDivert driver from loading. WinDivert is not a virus; it is flagged as a 'RiskTool' because it processes network packets.
causes: Antivirus programs such as Kaspersky, Norton, ESET, Bitdefender and Avast/AVG may block WinDivert.
steps: Verify that the files are official: Troubleshooting → Full check compares the SHA-256 hashes on the 'File integrity' line with the official GoodbyeDPI 0.2.3rc3 release.
Report the file to Microsoft as a false positive ('Report false positive' button → microsoft.com/wdsi/filesubmission); once it is reviewed and approved, Defender stops warning.
For other antivirus products (Kaspersky, Norton, ESET…) also use the vendor's 'report a false positive' page.
If a file was quarantined, restore it and start protection again.

Last resort: add only the NSF Shield folder (not the whole disk or Downloads) to the antivirus exclusions (Kaspersky: Settings → Threats and Exclusions → Manage exclusions; Norton: Items to Exclude from Scans.)
NSF-204.detect: Detected from the 'blocked by security software' text in GoodbyeDPI's output.

NSF-205.title: The Base Filtering Engine (BFE) is turned off
NSF-205.summary: The 'Base Filtering Engine' Windows service that WinDivert needs is not running.
causes: The service was disabled by an optimisation program or by a user.
steps: Try the 'Start BFE service' button below.
If that fails: Win+R → services.msc → 'Base Filtering Engine' → Startup type: Automatic → Start.
Restart the computer.
NSF-205.detect: Detected from GoodbyeDPI's output and, in the Find Problems scan, from the service status.

NSF-206.title: An incompatible WinDivert version is loaded
NSF-206.summary: A different WinDivert driver version loaded by another program is in memory.
causes: zapret, an old GoodbyeDPI version or another tool that uses WinDivert was run.
steps: Close the other programs that use WinDivert.
Press the 'Reset everything' button.
Restart the computer.
NSF-206.detect: Detected from the 'incompatible version' text in GoodbyeDPI's output.

NSF-207.title: An antivirus program was detected
NSF-207.summary: There is a third-party antivirus on your computer. If protection works without problems you do not need to do anything; if you get a driver error, follow the steps of NSF-204.
causes: Some antivirus programs block WinDivert or terminate GoodbyeDPI without notice.
steps: If it gets blocked, first report the file as a false positive (NSF-204).
If the antivirus 'scan encrypted connections' (HTTPS scanning) feature causes certificate errors, turn it off.
NSF-207.detect: Read from Windows Security Center during the Find Problems scan.

NSF-301.title: Another DPI tool is running
NSF-301.summary: A goodbyedpi.exe or winws.exe is running outside the app (for example old .cmd scripts or a zapret script). If two WinDivert tools run at the same time, connections break.
causes: One of the old scripts numbered 1-4, or a zapret script, was run.
Another GoodbyeDPI or zapret front-end is in use.
steps: Press the 'Resolve conflicts' button; NSF Shield closes the others and takes over.
NSF-301.detect: Running processes are checked every 3 seconds.

NSF-302.title: An old GoodbyeDPI service is installed
NSF-302.summary: There is a 'GoodbyeDPI' Windows service installed by the service_install scripts; it starts by itself when the computer boots and conflicts with NSF Shield.
causes: A service_install_*.cmd script was run earlier.
steps: Press the 'Resolve conflicts' button; the old service is removed.

NSF-303.title: Another DPI bypass tool is running
NSF-303.summary: Another blocking bypass program such as zapret (winws), ByeDPI, SpoofDPI or GreenTunnel is open. If two tools change packets at the same time, neither works properly.
causes: A previously installed blocking bypass tool is running in the background.
steps: Close the other tool (from Task Manager or from its own tray icon).
If necessary, remove that tool's service.
Restart NSF Shield protection.
NSF-303.detect: Running processes are checked during the Find Problems scan.

NSF-304.title: A VPN or proxy is active
NSF-304.summary: A VPN connection or a system proxy is on. If traffic goes through the VPN/proxy, GoodbyeDPI is not needed, and using both together can cause problems.
causes: A VPN program (WARP, Proton, Nord, WireGuard, OpenVPN…) is connected.
The Windows proxy setting is on.
steps: If you want to use the VPN, turn NSF Shield protection off; if you want to use NSF Shield, turn the VPN off.
If you do not use a proxy, turn it off in Settings → Network & internet → Proxy.
NSF-304.detect: Network adapters and the proxy setting are checked during the Find Problems scan.

NSF-401.title: There is DNS blocking
NSF-401.summary: Your provider's DNS server returns fake or empty addresses for blocked sites. In Turkey Discord is blocked this way; without DNS redirection Discord does not open.
causes: The provider blocks access at the DNS level.
steps: Use a profile that includes DNS redirection (e.g. 'Turkey – Recommended').
Alternative: change the Windows DNS server on the 'DNS Settings' page.
Then clear the DNS cache and restart Discord.
NSF-401.detect: With protection off, the system DNS answer is compared with independent DNS servers.

NSF-402.title: The redirected DNS server does not respond
NSF-402.summary: The DNS server used by the profile cannot be reached. In this case no site may open while protection is on.
causes: The DNS server is temporarily unreachable.
The provider or the modem blocks that port.
A firewall blocks UDP traffic.
steps: Run Internet Check → DNS Servers test.
Switch to a profile that uses a responding DNS (AdGuard, Quad9, OpenDNS).
The 'Find the best method' scan skips non-responding servers automatically.
NSF-402.detect: A test query is sent to the DNS server when protection starts.

NSF-403.title: Protection is on but the DNS answer is still wrong
NSF-403.summary: Although DNS redirection is on, Windows returns the blocked address.
causes: An old record remained in the Windows DNS cache.
The connection goes to the provider's DNS over IPv6.
A VPN or another DNS client interferes.
There is an entry in the hosts file.
steps: Clear the DNS cache.
Close Discord and the browser completely and open them again.
If the problem persists, change the Windows DNS on the 'DNS Settings' page.
NSF-403.detect: The system DNS answer is verified after protection starts.

NSF-404.title: IPv6 DNS queries are not redirected
NSF-404.summary: Your connection uses IPv6, but the selected profile only redirects IPv4 DNS queries. Windows may get a fake answer over IPv6.
causes: Only an IPv4 DNS address was entered in the custom profile.
steps: Use one of the built-in profiles (all of them redirect IPv6 too) or add an IPv6 DNS address to your custom profile.

NSF-405.title: The hosts file has a Discord entry
NSF-405.summary: An entry for Discord domains was found in the Windows hosts file. These entries override DNS and can point to old/wrong addresses.
causes: A previously tried 'unblocking' method added addresses to the hosts file.
steps: Open the file C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts with Notepad (as administrator).
Delete the lines that contain 'discord' or put # in front of them, then save.
Clear the DNS cache.
NSF-405.detect: The hosts file is read during the Find Problems scan.

NSF-501.title: DPI blocking could not be bypassed (connection is cut)
NSF-501.summary: The connection reaches the right server but is cut while the encrypted connection is being set up. The provider's DPI device recognises the method in use.
causes: The provider changed its DPI settings.
The selected method is ineffective on this line.
steps: Try all methods automatically with 'Find the best method'.
To try manually: the Automatic TTL, Single-byte Fragmentation and Strengthened Fake Packet profiles.
If targeted mode is on, turn it off and try again.
NSF-501.detect: Detected in the connection test from the TLS connection being reset.

NSF-502.title: Timeout (packets are being dropped)
NSF-502.summary: No answer comes from the server. The DPI device silently drops packets or your connection is very slow.
causes: The provider drops packets instead of resetting the connection.
The internet connection is very slow or down.
steps: Check that your internet connection works.
Run the 'Find the best method' scan.

NSF-503.title: IP blocking or the server is unreachable
NSF-503.summary: Even the correct IP address of the site cannot be reached. This may be IP blocking; GoodbyeDPI cannot bypass IP blocking.
causes: The provider blocked the server's IP address.
The server is temporarily down.
steps: Try again later.
Restart the modem.
Confirm the situation with Internet Check → Site Analysis.
If the IP blocking continues, only a VPN helps.

NSF-504.title: Certificate mismatch
NSF-504.summary: The server that was reached presented a different certificate. DNS gives a fake address or there is a program in between (antivirus HTTPS scanning, corporate proxy).
causes: DNS redirection is off or not working.
The antivirus scans encrypted connections.
The computer clock is wrong.
steps: Use a profile with DNS redirection and clear the DNS cache.
Turn off the antivirus 'scan encrypted connections' feature.
Check the computer's date and time.

NSF-505.title: Some servers open, others do not
NSF-505.summary: Part of Discord works but some servers (images, updates, chat connection) cannot be reached.
causes: The site list in targeted mode is incomplete.
Some servers are blocked with a different method.
steps: If targeted mode is on, complete the list with 'Add Discord addresses' or turn targeted mode off.
Run the 'Find the best method' scan with the 'try all methods' option.

NSF-506.title: The site that does not open is not in the target list
NSF-506.summary: Targeted mode is on and the server that does not open is not in the list, so no method is applied to it.
causes: A domain that was not added to the target site list is being used.
steps: Add the domain on the Target Sites page or turn targeted mode off.
Restart protection to apply the change.

NSF-601.title: The engine could not be started
NSF-601.summary: The engine closed right after it opened and did not give a recognised error message.
causes: An antivirus program terminated the process.
The driver could not be loaded.
The profile parameters are wrong.
steps: Look at the last GoodbyeDPI lines on the Log page.
Try a different profile.
Do 'Reset everything' and restart the computer.

NSF-602.title: The engine closed unexpectedly
NSF-602.summary: The engine process (goodbyedpi, winws or ciadpi) closed while protection was running.
causes: An antivirus program terminated the process.
The driver was reset while the computer woke from sleep.
It was closed from Task Manager.
steps: Keep 'Restart automatically if it closes' turned on in Settings.
If the antivirus closes it, report the file as a false positive (NSF-204).
Restart protection.

NSF-603.title: Invalid profile parameter
NSF-603.summary: The engine did not recognise a parameter in the profile.
causes: The custom profile contains a misspelled option or one that does not exist in this GoodbyeDPI version.
steps: Edit the profile on the Profiles page; check 'Extra parameters' and the manually written command.
Switch to a built-in profile.

NSF-604.title: The start-up message could not be read
NSF-604.summary: GoodbyeDPI is running but the 'Filter activated' message could not be read. Usually harmless.
causes: The computer is very busy or the console output arrived late.
steps: If the connection test succeeds, you do not need to do anything.

NSF-605.title: Unsafe parameter in the profile
NSF-605.summary: The selected profile contains a parameter that its engine does not know, an abbreviated one or an unsafe one (one that writes files or takes a free path); protection was not started with this profile.
causes: The profile was added from someone else's code or from a settings file.
The custom parameters were typed incorrectly (e.g. an abbreviation such as '--black').
The parameters contain command line characters (& | % " …).
steps: Edit the profile on the Profiles page; write each option separately and with its full name.
Or choose one of the built-in profiles.
NSF-605.detect: Parameters are checked against an allow-list when protection starts and when a profile code or settings file is imported.

NSF-701.title: The background service could not be installed
NSF-701.summary: GoodbyeDPI could not be installed as a Windows service.
causes: A broken service entry with the same name remained.
An antivirus prevented the service from being created.
steps: Press the 'Reset everything' button and restart the computer.
Or turn service mode off and use app mode.

NSF-702.title: The background service could not be started
NSF-702.summary: The service was installed but could not be started, or it stopped immediately.
causes: A driver error (usually the antivirus).
The app folder was moved.
steps: First start in app mode to see the error code.
Once the problem is solved, turn service mode on again.

NSF-703.title: The startup task could not be created
NSF-703.summary: The Task Scheduler task for 'Start with Windows' could not be created.
causes: The Task Scheduler service is turned off.
The app is in a temporary folder.
steps: Move the app to a permanent folder.
Turn the option off in Settings and on again.

NSF-704.title: The service points to an old folder
NSF-704.summary: The installed NSF Shield service runs GoodbyeDPI from a different location than the app's current folder (the app was moved or updated).
causes: The app folder was moved or the new version was extracted to a different folder.
steps: Press the 'Restart protection' button; the service is updated to point to the new folder.

NSF-705.title: Service and startup task are off in the portable version
NSF-705.summary: The background service (SYSTEM rights) and 'Start with Windows' (administrator rights without asking) can only be used in a version installed into an administrator-protected folder. Running with these rights from a folder that anyone can write to (Desktop, Downloads…) could let a malicious program on the computer gain those rights.
causes: The app runs from a portable folder extracted from the zip.
A service/task turned on by a previous version was removed for security.
steps: Protection works normally in app mode; as long as the app stays open (in the tray) you do not need to do anything.
To start it automatically at startup, install NSF Shield with the installer (Program Files).
NSF-705.detect: When the app starts, the folder permissions and the folder used by the installed service/task are checked.

NSF-801.title: No internet connection
NSF-801.summary: No public server (Cloudflare, Google, Quad9) can be reached; the problem is your connection, not blocking.
causes: The cable/Wi-Fi connection is down.
There is a fault at the modem or the provider.
steps: Turn protection off and check whether the internet works.
Turn the modem off and on again after 30 seconds.
Check the Wi-Fi/cable connection.

NSF-802.title: A system proxy is on
NSF-802.summary: A proxy server is set in Windows. Traffic that goes through the proxy may not be affected by GoodbyeDPI.
causes: A program or a user set a proxy.
steps: If you do not use a proxy, turn it off in Settings → Network & internet → Proxy.

NSF-803.title: The computer clock is wrong
NSF-803.summary: Your computer's clock is very different from the real time. Encrypted (HTTPS) connections give certificate errors.
causes: The time zone is wrong or automatic time is off.
The motherboard battery is empty.
steps: In the date and time settings turn on 'Set time automatically' and press 'Sync now'.

NSF-901.title: Discord was opened before protection
NSF-901.summary: Because Discord was opened while blocked, it may keep old connections and DNS records; it can get stuck on the 'Connecting…' screen.
causes: Discord started before NSF Shield when the computer booted.
Protection was started while Discord was open.
steps: Close Discord completely from its tray icon and open it again (or use the button below).
NSF-901.detect: When protection starts, Discord's start time is checked.

NSF-902.title: Discord is stuck on the update screen
NSF-902.summary: Discord cannot reach its update servers at start-up.
causes: updates.discord.com or dl.discordapp.net cannot be reached.
In targeted mode these addresses are not in the list.
steps: Check in the connection test that the 'updates.discord.com' server is reachable.
Turn targeted mode off or add the Discord addresses.
Restart Discord.

NSF-903.title: Discord cannot connect to voice chat
NSF-903.summary: Text chat works but voice stays on 'RTC connecting'. Discord voice servers use UDP; GoodbyeDPI does not change UDP traffic.
causes: The voice server's IP address is blocked or a device on the way restricts UDP.
steps: Discord → Settings → Voice & Video → turn off 'Enable Quality of Service High Packet Priority'.
Change the voice region (Rotterdam, Frankfurt…) in the server settings.
If the problem persists, only a VPN helps.

NSF-904.title: Opens in the browser, not in the app
NSF-904.summary: discord.com opens in the browser but the Discord app cannot connect.
causes: The app keeps old connections.
There is a proxy setting in Discord.
Discord is not up to date.
steps: Close Discord completely and open it again.
Clear the DNS cache.
Download Discord from the web again and install it.

NSF-805.title: Cannot connect to the proxy server
NSF-805.summary: A connection to the entered proxy address could not be made, or the server did not answer like a proxy.
causes: The IP address or port was typed wrong.
The proxy server is down (free proxies go down often).
The wrong proxy type was chosen (SOCKS5 instead of HTTP or the other way round).
The proxy's IP address is blocked too.
steps: Check the address and port (e.g. 185.12.34.56:8080).
Change the type (HTTP ↔ SOCKS5) and test again.
Try another proxy.
Paste the details from your proxy provider as they are into the 'Quick entry' box.
NSF-805.detect: Detected with the 'Test' button on the Proxy page.

NSF-806.title: Wrong proxy user name/password
NSF-806.summary: The proxy server requires authentication and the entered details were not accepted.
causes: The user name or password is wrong.
The proxy subscription has expired.
The proxy only allows certain IP addresses.
steps: Check the user name and password and enter them again.
Add your own IP to the IP allow-list in your proxy provider's panel.

NSF-807.title: The proxy cannot reach Discord
NSF-807.summary: The proxy works, but an encrypted connection to Discord could not be made through it.
causes: Discord is blocked in the proxy's country too.
The proxy does not allow tunnels to port 443.
The proxy alters the traffic (the certificate does not match).
steps: Try a proxy in another country.
Use an HTTP proxy that supports HTTPS/CONNECT or a SOCKS5 proxy.

NSF-107.title: The engine cannot run on this Windows
NSF-107.summary: Zapret (winws) and ByeDPI (ciadpi) are shipped for 64-bit Windows only.
causes: The computer runs 32-bit Windows.
steps: Use the GoodbyeDPI engine (Profiles → GoodbyeDPI); it has a 32-bit version too.

NSF-606.title: A site list cannot be used by this engine
NSF-606.summary: The Exclude list is on, but GoodbyeDPI has no exclude list; the list was not applied.
causes: GoodbyeDPI 0.2.3rc3 only has an include list (--blacklist).
steps: Switch to Zapret or ByeDPI (Profiles page or tray menu) to use the Exclude list.
Or turn the Exclude list off on the Site Lists page.

NSF-808.title: ByeDPI port is in use
NSF-808.summary: ByeDPI could not listen on its local port (127.0.0.1), or its local bridge could not be opened.
causes: Another program (another proxy or a ByeDPI copy) uses the same port.
An antivirus or firewall blocked ciadpi.exe.
steps: Choose another ByeDPI port in Settings (for example 18990) and start again.
Close other proxy programs.
Check the antivirus quarantine for ciadpi.exe.

NSF-809.title: The Windows proxy was not set for ByeDPI
NSF-809.summary: ByeDPI runs, but the Windows proxy points to your own proxy or could not be changed, so browsers do not use ByeDPI.
causes: A proxy from the Proxy page is set as the Windows proxy.
The proxy setting is managed by a company policy.
steps: Turn off the Windows proxy on the Proxy page and restart protection.
Or use per-program rules with 'ByeDPI engine' on the Proxy page.

Yandex.note: The server used by the old scripts 3/4. Because it is in Russia its answers are a little slow (~100 ms) but it is very stable.

AdGuard.note: Very fast (~20 ms). Also blocks ad and tracker domains; ad areas may look empty on some sites.

AdGuardFree.name: AdGuard Unfiltered
AdGuardFree.note: AdGuard's version that blocks nothing. It is fast.

Quad9.note: Based in Switzerland, privacy-focused and fast. Only blocks malware sites.

OpenDns.note: Cisco's DNS service. Fast and stable.

Cloudflare.note: Uses the standard port 53. Useless if your provider interferes with traffic on port 53; the scan checks this by itself.

Google.note: Uses the standard port 53. In Turkey, queries to this address were redirected in the past; it is not reliable on its own.

tr-recommended.name: Turkey – Recommended
tr-recommended.description: First choice for Discord. The most complete mode (-9) + Yandex DNS redirection. Same setting as the old scripts 3 and 4.

tr-adguard.name: Turkey – AdGuard DNS
tr-adguard.description: -9 mode + AdGuard DNS (port 5353). Answers much faster than Yandex; also blocks ad domains.

tr-quad9.name: Turkey – Quad9 DNS
tr-quad9.description: -9 mode + Quad9 DNS (port 9953). Fast and privacy-focused, no ad filter.

tr-opendns.name: Turkey – OpenDNS
tr-opendns.description: -9 mode + OpenDNS (port 5353). Try it if the other DNS servers are slow or do not respond.

tr-autottl.name: Automatic TTL (-5)
tr-autottl.description: Sets the TTL of fake packets automatically from the distance to the server. Try it if the fixed-TTL methods stopped working.

tr-legacy1-dns.name: Old Script 1 + DNS (TTL 3)
tr-legacy1-dns.description: 1_bunu_dene.cmd with DNS redirection added: only TTL 3 fake packets + Yandex DNS.

tr-legacy2-dns.name: Old Script 2 + DNS (-4, TTL 5)
tr-legacy2-dns.description: 2_bunu_dene.cmd with DNS redirection added: -4 mode + TTL 5 fake packets + Yandex DNS.

tr-wrongseq.name: Wrong Sequence Number (-6)
tr-wrongseq.description: Sends fake packets with a past TCP sequence number. On some modems it is more stable than -9.

tr-wrongchk.name: Wrong Checksum (-7)
tr-wrongchk.description: Sends fake packets with a wrong TCP checksum. May not work in virtual machines and on some modems.

tr-mode8.name: Sequence + Checksum (-8)
tr-mode8.description: Uses the -6 and -7 methods together; there is no QUIC blocking (its only difference from -9).

tr-fakegen.name: Strengthened Fake Packet
tr-fakegen.description: -9 mode + 5 random fake packets. For providers that apply strict DPI.

tr-resend.name: Repeated Fake Packet
tr-resend.description: -9 mode + 3 fake packets, each sent 3 times. More reliable on lines with packet loss (Wi-Fi, mobile).

tr-e1.name: Single-byte Fragmentation
tr-e1.description: -9 mode, but the first HTTPS packet is split into 1-byte pieces. DPI cannot read the site name at all; opening connections gets a little slower.

tr-sni.name: Split at Site Name (SNI)
tr-sni.description: -9 mode + splits the packet exactly where the site name (SNI) starts. The site name falls into two separate packets.

tr-native.name: Plain-order Fragmentation
tr-native.description: Same as -9, but the fragments are sent in normal instead of reverse order. For networks that do not accept reverse-ordered fragments.

tr-alt.name: Alternative (-5 + 1 byte + fake)
tr-alt.description: Automatic TTL + 1-byte fragmentation + 5 fake packets + QUIC blocking. The method from GoodbyeDPI's 'ALT' scripts.

tr-compatible.name: Most Compatible Classic (-1)
tr-compatible.description: Classic method without fake packets: splits packets into 2-byte pieces. Slow but works on every network.

tr-classic2.name: Classic Fast (-2)
tr-classic2.description: Faster version of -1: HTTPS is split into 40-byte pieces.

dns-only.name: DNS Redirection Only
dns-only.description: Applies no DPI trick, only redirects DNS. The lightest option if your provider blocks only via DNS.

legacy-1.name: Old Script 1 (TTL 3, no DNS)
legacy-1.description: Exactly the same as 1_bunu_dene.cmd. Because it has no DNS redirection it does not open Discord in Turkey; for comparison.

legacy-2.name: Old Script 2 (-4, TTL 5, no DNS)
legacy-2.description: Exactly the same as 2_bunu_dene.cmd. Because it has no DNS redirection it does not open Discord in Turkey; for comparison.

plain.name: Plain (-9, no DNS)
plain.description: Only the -9 mode. May be enough if you changed the Windows DNS on the 'DNS Settings' page.

zapret-discord.name: Discord + Web (TLS + QUIC)
zapret-discord.description: Recommended Zapret profile: HTTPS with a fake ClientHello and split, QUIC (UDP 443) and Discord voice (UDP 50000-50100).

zapret-aggressive.name: Aggressive ISP
zapret-aggressive.description: More repeats, more split points and a modified fake packet, for providers where the recommended profile is not enough.

zapret-tls.name: TLS only
zapret-tls.description: Only HTTPS (TCP 443) with a fake packet and split; the lightest, no UDP.

zapret-split.name: Compatible (split only)
zapret-split.description: Splits the first packet without fake packets, for networks that drop fake packets.

byedpi-recommended.name: Recommended (split)
byedpi-recommended.description: ByeDPI's recommended Windows setting. First tried: split at SNI+1 and disorder at SNI+3 (HTTP: Host header case and space). Fallback group (on reset or timeout): a TLS record split at SNI+1.

byedpi-fake.name: Fake packet
byedpi-fake.description: One group, no fallback: disorder at 1 and a fake first part sent with TTL 8 before the real data.

byedpi-tlsrec.name: TLS record + split (no TTL)
byedpi-tlsrec.description: First tried: split at SNI+1 with a TLS record split at SNI+3. Fallback group (no answer within 3 s, or reset): disorder at 1 with a record split at SNI+1. No fake packets or TTL tricks.

byedpi-oob.name: Out-of-band (OOB)
byedpi-oob.description: First tried: split at SNI+1 with an out-of-band byte at SNI+3. Fallback group (on reset or timeout): disorder at SNI+3.

zapret-general.name: Web (fakedsplit, auto TTL)
zapret-general.description: General web traffic: QUIC (UDP 443) with fake Initial packets; HTTP and HTTPS with a fake packet and a split ClientHello (fakedsplit), TTL set automatically. The Discord voice ports are not captured.

zapret-ttl.name: Fixed TTL (fake + split)
zapret-ttl.description: Fake packets with a fixed TTL of 4 (they expire before the server) and a split at the SNI, for HTTP, HTTPS and QUIC. Try it when the profiles with an automatic TTL do not work.

zapret-voice.name: Discord voice (STUN / IP discovery)
zapret-voice.description: Discord voice first: fake IP discovery and STUN packets on UDP 50000-50100, plus light QUIC and HTTPS rules. Whether voice works depends on the network; the scanner does not measure it.

zapret-light.name: Low intervention (TLS reorder)
zapret-light.description: The smallest change: only TCP 443, the first part of the ClientHello is sent out of order. No fake packets, no UDP.

zapret-lastresort.name: Last resort (heavy)
zapret-lastresort.description: Many fake packets with a wrong sequence and checksum, fakeddisorder on HTTP and HTTPS, fakes for QUIC and Discord voice. More traffic and more side effects; use it only when the others fail.

byedpi-tlsrec-only.name: TLS record split only
byedpi-tlsrec-only.description: First tried: the TLS ClientHello is split into two TLS records at SNI+1. Fallback group (on reset or timeout): the split at SNI+3. No other method and no HTTP change.

byedpi-hybrid-oob.name: Hybrid OOB (disoob + TLS record)
byedpi-hybrid-oob.description: First tried: disorder with an out-of-band byte (disoob) and a TLS record split at SNI+1. Fallback group (on reset or timeout): OOB at SNI+3 with a record split at SNI+3.

byedpi-http-https.name: HTTP and HTTPS separately
byedpi-http-https.description: HTTP connections: split at the Host and Host header tricks (case, space). HTTPS connections use the second group (the first is limited to HTTP): split + disorder at the SNI and a TLS record split.

intro.title: How to use this window
intro.text:
Point at or click an option; what it does is explained here.

Your provider blocks Discord in two layers:
1) DNS: it gives a wrong answer to the question 'where is discord.com?'.
2) DPI: it reads the site name (SNI) in the first packet of the connection and cuts the connection.

DNS redirection bypasses the first layer, the DPI methods below bypass the second. In Turkey both are needed together.

name.title: Profile name and description
name.text: Helps you recognise the profile in the list. It has no effect on the command line.

mode.title: Base mode
mode.text:
Selects one of GoodbyeDPI's ready-made method sets. A mode turns on several of the options below at once.

• Modern modes (-5 … -9): split the packets and send 'fake' packets to fool the DPI device. They give the best results in Turkey.
• Classic modes (-1 … -4): only split the packets and play with the HTTP headers. They are more compatible but weak against current DPI systems.

If you choose a mode and also tick options, the options are added on top of the mode.

modeNone.title: No mode
modeNone.text: No ready-made set is used; only the options you tick below are applied. Leave the mode empty if you only want DNS redirection.

mode1.title: -1 · Classic, most compatible
mode1.text: Splits HTTP and HTTPS packets into 2-byte pieces and makes small changes to the HTTP headers. Sends no fake packets. Works on every network but is the slowest mode and may not get past strict DPI.

mode2.title: -2 · Classic, faster for HTTPS
mode2.text: Same as -1 but HTTPS packets are split into 40-byte pieces; connections open faster.

mode3.title: -3 · Classic, fast HTTP/HTTPS
mode3.text: No fragmentation of persistent HTTP connections; even faster.

mode4.title: -4 · Classic, fastest
mode4.text: Only header tricks for unencrypted HTTP. It does not touch HTTPS (including Discord); on its own it is not enough for Discord. The old script number 2 combined it with TTL 5 fake packets.

mode5.title: -5 · Modern, automatic TTL
mode5.text: Sets the lifetime (TTL) of the fake packets automatically on every connection, based on the distance to the server. When fixed-TTL methods break over time (as the old scripts 1 and 2 did), this is the most robust option.

mode6.title: -6 · Modern, wrong sequence number
mode6.text: Fake packets are sent with a past TCP sequence number; the server ignores them while the DPI reads them and is fooled.

mode7.title: -7 · Modern, wrong checksum
mode7.text: Fake packets are sent with a broken checksum. Some modems and virtual machines drop these packets on the way, so it may have no effect.

mode8.title: -8 · Modern, sequence + checksum
mode8.text: -6 and -7 used together. The only difference from -9 is that it does not block QUIC.

mode9.title: -9 · Modern, full (default)
mode9.text: GoodbyeDPI's default and most complete mode. This is the recommended mode for Discord in Turkey.

ttl.title: Fake packet TTL (lifetime)
ttl.text:
The fake packet must reach the provider's DPI device but 'die' before it reaches the real server. The TTL sets how many routers the packet can pass.

• Too small and it does not even reach the DPI device → no effect.
• Too big and it reaches the server → the connection breaks.
• 'Automatic' measures the distance on every connection and picks a suitable value; it keeps working even when the provider changes its network.

The old script 1 used TTL 3 and script 2 used TTL 5; fixed values can stop working over time.

fakegen.title: Number of fake packets
fakegen.text:
This many fake packets filled with random data are sent ahead of the real connection. The DPI device takes the fake packets for real ones and reads the wrong site name.

0 = GoodbyeDPI's default single fake packet. 3-10 helps on lines with strict DPI; a very high value slows down opening connections. At most 30.

fakeresend.title: Fake packet repeats
fakeresend.text: Sends every fake packet this many times. On connections with packet loss, such as Wi-Fi or mobile lines, it makes sure the DPI device sees the fake packet. 1 = no repeat.

dns.title: DNS redirection
dns.text:
Sends every DNS query your computer makes (port 53) to a different port of the selected server instead of your provider's server.

In Turkey Discord is also blocked at the DNS level, so this option is REQUIRED: if it is off, Discord does not open (this is why the old scripts 1 and 2 did not work).

Providers only inspect port 53, so queries to ports such as 1253, 5353 or 9953 are not blocked. All ready-made choices redirect IPv6 queries too.

dnsCustom.title: Custom DNS server
dnsCustom.text:
Enter your own DNS server. Choose a server that uses a non-standard port; port 53 can be redirected by the provider.

If you have an IPv6 connection, enter the IPv6 address too; otherwise Windows may ask the provider's DNS over IPv6 and get a fake answer (NSF-404).

httpsfrag.title: HTTPS piece size
httpsfrag.text:
Into how many bytes the first packet of the encrypted connection (which contains the site name) is split. If the DPI device cannot see the site name in one piece, it cannot block it.

1-2: most effective but opening a connection gets a little slower. 40: faster, some DPIs may catch it. 0 = the mode's default.

httpfrag.title: HTTP piece size
httpfrag.text: Piece size of unencrypted HTTP requests. Discord and almost all sites use HTTPS, so its effect is small. 0 = the mode's default.

wrongchk.title: Wrong checksum
wrongchk.text:
Sends the fake packets with a wrong TCP checksum. The real server throws these packets away; the DPI device usually reads them without checking and is fooled.

Some modems and virtual machines (VirtualBox/VMware NAT) drop broken packets on the way, so it may have no effect.

wrongseq.title: Wrong sequence number
wrongseq.text: Sends the fake packets with a past TCP sequence/acknowledgement number. The server ignores them as 'old packets'; the DPI device looks at the content and reads the wrong site name. Usually the most reliable fake packet method.

native.title: Native fragmentation
native.text: Really sends the first packet as separate small TCP packets. It does not shrink the window size, so it does not slow the connection down.

reverse.title: Reverse-order fragmentation
reverse.text: Sends the pieces in reverse order (the last piece first). DPI devices cannot put reversed pieces together and cannot read the site name. Very rarely a site cannot handle the reverse order; if there is a problem, turn it off and use 'Native fragmentation'.

quic.title: Block QUIC/HTTP3
quic.text: Blocks the QUIC/HTTP3 (UDP 443) traffic browsers use. The browser falls back to normal HTTPS, which GoodbyeDPI can handle. Recommended; it does not affect Discord voice chat.

sni.title: Split at the site name (SNI)
sni.text: Splits the first packet exactly where the site name starts; the site name ends up in two separate packets. A more targeted split, independent of the -e value.

payload.title: Skip large packets
payload.text: Does not process packets carrying more than 1200 bytes of data (file downloads, video streams). Reduces CPU usage; does not affect bypassing blocks. Already on in the modern modes.

nosni.title: Also apply when the site name cannot be read
nosni.text: Only matters while 'Targeted mode' is on: also applies the method to connections whose site name cannot be read (e.g. those using encrypted SNI/ECH).

passive.title: Block passive DPI
passive.text: Catches and drops the fake 'redirect' (HTTP 302) and connection reset packets the provider injects. On in the classic modes.

hostr.title: Host → hoSt
hostr.text: Writes the 'Host' header of unencrypted HTTP requests as 'hoSt'; old DPI systems do not recognise the header. No effect on HTTPS.

hosts.title: Remove the Host space
hosts.text: Removes the space in the HTTP 'Host:' header. Unencrypted HTTP only.

hostm.title: Mix the Host letter case
hostm.text: Mixes upper and lower case in the site name (dIsCoRd.CoM). Unencrypted HTTP only.

extra.title: Extra parameters
extra.text:
For adding GoodbyeDPI options that are not listed above by hand. Examples:
• --min-ttl 3 : send the fake packet only to servers at least 3 hops away
• --fake-from-hex 1603… : set the fake packet content yourself
• --port 8443 : also fragment on an extra TCP port

Do not add --blacklist; use the 'Target Sites' page for that.

aboutPage.title: About
aboutPage.intro: An easy-to-use internet access shield for GoodbyeDPI, Zapret and ByeDPI. It bypasses the blocks providers apply with DNS and Deep Packet Inspection (DPI). It is not a VPN: your traffic is not encrypted and your IP address does not change.
aboutPage.how: Your provider blocks Discord in two ways: by changing DNS answers and by reading the site name (SNI) in the connection and cutting it. DNS redirection sends the queries to an unblocked DNS server; GoodbyeDPI splits the packets and sends fake packets so that the DPI device cannot read the site name.
aboutPage.antivirus: Antivirus warning: WinDivert is a network driver; some antivirus programs (Kaspersky, Norton…) may flag it as 'RiskTool'. It is not a virus; Troubleshooting → Full check verifies that the files are the official ones. If you get a warning, first report it to Microsoft as a false positive (NSF-204).
aboutPage.thirdParty: The bundled components are covered by their own licenses: GoodbyeDPI © ValdikSS (Apache 2.0), WinDivert © basil00 (LGPLv3). Texts: the Licenses button.
aboutPage.thanks: Thanks: GoodbyeDPI – ValdikSS (Apache 2.0) · WinDivert – basil00 (LGPLv3) · uthash, getline.

engineEdit.helpSafety: For your safety only full option names are accepted; options that write files or take a file path are refused. Payloads are chosen by name; the Include/Exclude lists are added by the app.

help.zapret: winws (zapret) captures traffic with the WinDivert driver. --wf-tcp and --wf-udp choose the captured ports. Every rule starts with --filter-tcp, --filter-udp or --filter-l7, and --new starts the next rule. Common methods: --dpi-desync=fake,multisplit or fake,multidisorder with --dpi-desync-split-pos and --dpi-desync-fooling=badseq,md5sig.
help.byedpi: ByeDPI (ciadpi) is a local SOCKS proxy and needs no driver. Write the options as --name value. --split, --disorder, --fake, --oob and --tlsrec take a position such as 1+s (counted from the SNI). --auto=torst starts a group that is tried only when a connection is reset or times out.

zapret.rulesText: Every rule handles part of the traffic (for example QUIC, Discord voice, HTTP, HTTPS) with its own method.
zapret.voiceText: The Discord IP discovery and STUN packets of voice and video calls are handled too (UDP 50000-50100).
zapret.quicText: UDP 443 (QUIC) connections get fake initial packets, so browsers do not fall back slowly.
zapret.driverText: Uses its own signed WinDivert 2.2.2 driver (bin\zapret); the GoodbyeDPI driver is unloaded when you switch.
